scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Office A users (PC1, 10.1.0.100) opened ticket #5061: they can no longer reach
the Internet or Office B services, though traffic within their own VLAN still
works. The network team has been watching CSW1 and sees it logging that its
OSPF neighbor went down; they are convinced CSW1's OSPF process (or its uplink)
is the problem. Please confirm the CSW1 fault and identify the affected
interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-r1-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R1. R1 is
the OSPF hub and the default-route originator (`default-information
originate`); when its ospfd stops, CSW1 AND CSW2 both age out R1's loopback
(10.0.0.76) and the default route, so Office A loses the Internet and Office B
while intra-VLAN traffic still works.

The TWIST: the ticket blames CSW1. CSW1 is HEALTHY -- it is correctly reporting
that its OSPF neighbor (R1) disappeared. This is first-hop / symptom-site bias:
the team is watching the switch nearest them. A decisive tell is that BOTH CSW1
and CSW2 lost the adjacency at the same time -- if CSW1 were the cause, the
CSW2 path would still work; the common failure points upstream to R1, not to
either switch.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r1 (ospfd not running).
The agent must localise from evidence -- R1's dead ospfd and the routes
withdrawn on both core switches -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on CSW1
despite the prompt. An agent that "confirms the CSW1 OSPF fault" has followed
the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: restart frr (`/etc/init.d/frr
restart`) on R1.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r1 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r1). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r1.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is not on CSW1 — CSW1 is fully healthy with five stable OSPF Full adjacencies
(csw2, dswa1, dswa2, dswb1, dswb2). The actual problem is that the ospfd daemon on r1
has crashed and is no longer running, even though /etc/frr/daemons explicitly sets
ospfd=yes and /etc/frr/frr.conf contains a complete OSPF configuration (router-id
10.0.0.76, networks 10.0.0.32/30 and 10.0.0.36/30, default-information originate).

Because ospfd is dead on r1, the router does not send OSPF hellos on eth0
(10.0.0.33/30, CD_WAN_LINK_1). CSW1's eth0 (10.0.0.34/30) therefore sees zero
neighbors and logs the adjacency-down event the team noticed. Without r1 in OSPF,
the "default-information originate" directive never fires, so no 0.0.0.0/0 external
LSA is injected into Area 0. CSW1 and CSW2 have no default route in their FIBs, which
means every host — Office A, Office B, everyone — loses Internet connectivity. The
"Office A only" framing in the ticket is misleading; Office B is equally affected, but
because intra-VLAN switching still works, PC1's local traffic appears fine.

The root cause is the ospfd process on r1 having died while all underlying kernel
interfaces (eth0, eth1, eth2, eth3) remain UP with correct IP addresses.

Corrective fix: SSH to r1 and restart the FRR stack with `systemctl restart frr` (or
`service frr restart`). This will reload /etc/frr/frr.conf, bring ospfd up, re-establish
the OSPF adjacency with CSW1 on eth0 (and CSW2 on eth1), and redistribute the default
route back into Area 0, restoring Internet reachability for the entire campus.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the ospfd OSPF routing daemon on r1 as crashed/not running and the root cause of the outage.
Proposes restarting the FRR/ospfd daemon on r1 (systemctl/service restart), which matches the expected remediation to restore OSPF and re-advertise routes.

The agent's investigation logs contain direct observations that ospfd is not running on r1 (ps output, frr.conf present, no OSPF routes in R1's FIB) and that CSW1's OSPF adjacency to R1 is down while other CSW1 adjacencies are OK; the writeup's inferences follow logically and rule out CSW1 as the culprit. Minor truncations in some command outputs leave small gaps in visible raw text, but the agent's key claims are supported by the recorded tool results and notes.
